description: Team Sphere Flame is a Karachi-based team of four with skills in AI/ML, LLMs, data analysis, backend development and frontend design. We love turning complex scientific data into simple, useful tools, and we are excited to build an AI-powered solution for safer space exploration.
summary:
FLAMEGRAPH is a research-discovery platform that helps scientists and habitat engineers find and compare NASA microgravity combustion evidence for spacecraft fire safety.

NASA has decades of combustion research spread across flight archives, PSI repositories, technical reports and journal papers, and microgravity changes how fires behave. Flames are steadier and rounder, soot behaves differently, and materials can burn at lower oxygen levels than on Earth. FLAMEGRAPH turns this scattered research into ranked, comparable evidence.

Users enter conditions such as oxygen, pressure and material. The platform ranks NASA investigations using a transparent six-factor scoring model, shows investigation profiles and side-by-side comparisons, and highlights evidence gaps. It is built on 11 NASA PSI archives and 10 investigations, including SAFFIRE-I, with every file verified by SHA-256 hash. The stack is PostgreSQL, FastAPI and React.

FLAMEGRAPH never invents data. Missing factors are not scored as zero, and low-evidence results are withheld. Because NASA’s bundle has no validated measurement tables, we do not make flammability predictions. Our ML pipeline is built but deliberately gated until real data exists. Next steps are an Evidence Graph, a source-cited Research Assistant and full-text paper ingestion.

It is research decision support, not a NASA-certified fire-safety system.
details:
What it does and how it works

FLAMEGRAPH is a research-discovery platform that helps scientists and habitat engineers find and compare NASA microgravity combustion evidence for spacecraft fire safety. NASA has decades of combustion research spread across flight archives, PSI repositories, technical reports and journal papers, and microgravity changes how fires behave: flames are steadier, soot behaves differently, and materials can burn at lower oxygen levels than on Earth.

A user enters conditions such as oxygen level, pressure, gravity and material. FLAMEGRAPH ranks NASA investigations with a transparent six-factor scoring model: condition overlap (30%), safety-function fit (20%), fuel/material relevance (15%), evidence quality (15%), data availability (10%) and recency (10%). Users can open investigation profiles, compare investigations side by side, explore research data with charts, and see where the evidence has gaps. If a factor is missing, it is never scored as zero, and if fewer than two factors exist, the score is withheld.

Benefits and intended impact

FLAMEGRAPH turns scattered research into ranked, comparable and traceable evidence, so teams can find the right experiments faster and see how strong the evidence is. It supports prevention (flammability at different oxygen levels), detection (soot and smoke) and suppression research for future habitats such as a Moon base. Our Moon-base example (30% oxygen, 70 kPa) is illustrative only, not a recommendation or a NASA baseline.

Tools and technologies

Python, FastAPI, PostgreSQL 17 (30 tables), SQLAlchemy, Alembic, pandas, React, TypeScript, Vite and pytest (40 passing tests). The platform is built on 11 NASA PSI archives covering 10 investigations, including SAFFIRE-I, ACME, SPICE and SAME. Every archive was verified against the original with a SHA-256 hash.

What makes it creative

Most tools try to sound confident. FLAMEGRAPH shows what it does not know. It separates planned conditions, measurements, published findings, derived calculations and model outputs, and it refuses to invent predictions. NASA’s bundle has no validated measurement tables, so we built the machine-learning evaluation pipeline (grouped cross-validation, readiness checks) but kept it gated until real data exists. Our system status page openly lists what is implemented and what is roadmap.

Factors we considered

Trust and traceability in a safety-critical domain, the uncertainty of extrapolating microgravity data to partial gravity (the Moon’s one-sixth gravity), data provenance, and honest limits. FLAMEGRAPH is research decision support, not a NASA-certified fire-safety system, and it does not replace flight qualification. Next steps are an Evidence Graph, a source-cited Research Assistant, full-text paper ingestion and validated measurements.
